_doc: What heroes say on the road and in the dark, by voice: a hero speaks with the first of their traits (then their temper) that has lines for the moment, or 'any'. {name} is the speaker, {who} the hero it is about, {nick} their nickname, {site} the place. Lines are picked without dice, so they never change how a delve goes.

hottempered: "Last one to the {site} buys the ale," {name} says, already walking.
{name} wants to march through the night. Nobody else does.
shy: {name} checks the straps on every pack twice and says nothing at all.
{name} walks at the back, where nobody will ask them anything.
greedy: "They say there's a hoard in the {site}," {name} says, for the fourth time today.
{name} has already counted the bounty out loud, split four ways and then three.
generous: {name} shares out the last of the honey cakes before the gate is out of sight.
{name} gives their good cloak to a beggar at the gate and walks out cold.
gregarious: {name} sings the whole first mile, badly, and makes the others join the chorus.
{name} tells the one about the dwarf and the mule again. It gets a laugh again.
ambitious: "They'll be singing about this one," {name} promises.
{name} has already decided what the bards will call it.
lazy: {name} asks, twice, whether there's a shorter road.
{name} is the last to the gate, still chewing breakfast.
romantic: {name} waves at someone in a window long after the gate closes behind them.
pious: {name} touches the shrine by the gate and asks for a safe road.
bold: "Whatever's in there, it's never met us," {name} says.

hottempered: "Mine," {name} growls, and charges before anyone can stop them.
shy: {name} goes very quiet and finds a spot behind the others.
greedy: "Look behind it. Look at the gold," {name} whispers.
ambitious: "This is the one they'll sing about," {name} says, and draws.
lazy: "Can we not just leave it here?" {name} asks. Nobody answers.
gregarious: {name} shouts a greeting at it, which nobody else thinks was wise.
pious: {name} speaks a prayer into the dark before the first blow.
merciful: "Last chance to walk away," {name} calls to it. It doesn't.
bold: {name} steps out in front of the others.

gregarious: {name} whoops loud enough to wake the whole place.
greedy: "Do that again and I'll stand you a drink," {name} tells {who}.

gregarious: {name} laughs until they have to sit down.
"I'm telling everyone about that," {name} says. They will.
generous: {name} helps {who} pick it back up and says nothing about it.
any: {name} pretends not to have seen that.

hottempered: "{who}!" {name} roars, and goes at the thing twice as hard.
{name} sees {who} fall and stops thinking at all.
shy: {name} goes white and stands over {who} without a word.
greedy: {name} grabs {who}'s purse before anyone else can. To keep it safe, they say.

hottempered: {name} has to be dragged away, still swearing at it.
ambitious: "We'll be back," {name} says, mostly to the dark.
{name} looks back the whole way out.
lazy: "Told you we should've stayed home," {name} pants.
shy: {name} is first through the door, and doesn't apologise for it.

gregarious: {name} starts a victory song before the last one has stopped twitching.
greedy: {name} is already going through their pockets.
lazy: {name} sits down right where they are and refuses to move for a while.
pious: {name} says a word for the dead, theirs and the enemy's.
any: {name} wipes their blade and breathes again.

greedy: {name} bites every coin to be sure.
"Right. Nobody touch anything," says {name}, touching everything.
generous: {name} sets a share aside for the folk back home.
gregarious: {name} is already planning the round they'll buy with it.

hottempered: {name} doesn't cry. {name} goes back in alone, and has to be pulled out again.
{name} breaks their sword on the wall and doesn't say why.
shy: {name} sits with {who} a long time and says nothing at all.
{name} closes {who}'s eyes and keeps their ring.
gregarious: {name} tries to tell the one about the mule, the way {who} told it, and can't finish.
{name} talks to {who} the whole way home, as if they were listening.
generous: {name} wraps {who} in their own good cloak for the road home.
greedy: {name} doesn't take {who}'s purse. That is how the others know how bad it is.
pious: {name} says the words for the dead over {who}, and gets them all right.
any: {name} carries {who} the whole way home and won't let anyone help.

potion: {name} knocks back a {potion} between blows (+{hp} hp).
{name} drains a {potion} and spits out the cork (+{hp} hp).
over: It takes {rounds}, and then it's quiet.
{Rounds} of blood and noise, then nothing.

fumble.named: The {party} have started calling {name} "{nick}". {name} has stopped pretending to mind.
tease: "Hold on to it this time, {nick}," {name} says.
Somebody shouts "{nick}!" and everyone but {who} laughs.

down.named: Knocked flat so often and still breathing, {name} is "{nick}" to the {party} now.
tease: "Up you get, {nick}," {name} says. "You've done this before."

crit.named: After one perfect blow too many, the {party} call {name} "{nick}".

potion.named: {name} drinks more healing potions than anyone alive, and the {party} have started calling them "{nick}".
tease: "Easy, {nick}, save some for the rest of us," {name} says.

groan: {names} put their heads in their hands.

funeral.wake: There is nobody to bury. {town} holds a wake at the tavern for {name}, and {speaker} pours one out for {them}.

hottempered: "{who} never once waited for the plan," {name} says. "I hope wherever they are, nobody makes them."
"Whatever did this, I'll find it," is all {name} says, and walks out before the last hymn.
shy: "{who} was my friend," {name} says. Then nothing more, and nobody needs more.
{name} leaves something small on the grave and won't say what it was.
gregarious: "{who} owed me four silver and a song. I'll take the song." And {name} sings it.
{name} tells the story of the night {who} fell in the river, and the whole room laughs and cries at once.
generous: "{who} gave away everything they had," {name} says. "Even this, in the end."
{name} pays for the stone out of their own purse.
greedy: "{who} never stood a round in their life," {name} says. "I'd stand them every one now."
{name} counts {who}'s share of the last job onto the grave, coin by coin, and leaves it there.
ambitious: "{who} wanted the bards to know their name," {name} says. "I'll see they do."
lazy: "{who} always took the first watch so I wouldn't have to," {name} says, and can't go on.
romantic: {name} reads a letter {who} never sent, and nobody asks who it was for.
pious: "{who} walked the road the gods set them," {name} says, "all the way to the end."
{name} says the old words over {who}, and gets every one of them right.
merciful: "{who} would have spared the thing that killed them," {name} says. "That's who they were."
bold: "{who} went first. Always first," {name} says. "Somebody has to now."
any: "{who} kept watch for us every night," {name} says. "Rest now. We'll keep it."
"Safe road, {who}," {name} says, and that is all.

funeral.vow: {speaker} swears on {name}'s grave to see {site} cleared.
funeral.vowWake: {speaker} swears on {name}'s memory to see {site} cleared.
funeral.kept: {speaker} stands at {name}'s grave and tells them {site} is cleared. The vow is kept.
funeral.keptBy: Word comes that {site} has fallen to others. {speaker} goes to {name}'s grave all the same, and lets the vow go.
